business_problem: When the feature request came in, Notion's mobile app already had a functional version, but the desktop and web client didn't. Even though Ryan wasn't entirely sure how the feature worked on mobile, he was able to give the problem to Codex.
solution_summary: When the feature request came in, Notion's mobile app already had a functional version, but the desktop and web client didn't. Even though Ryan wasn't entirely sure how the feature worked on mobile, he was able to give the problem to Codex. He pointed it at the mobile codebase, gave it a clear description of how it would need to look on the web, and provided a way to verify the result. Codex came back with a complete first cut of the web implementation, in one shot, that matched Notion's codebase conventions closely enough to ship the next day. At Notion, Codex is changing how engineers build. The company is rethinking the software primitives and abstractions it builds so that agents can use them.
